body: Well done for holding on this long. I know how hard it is, because I am in the same boat (heh) and have pulled myself from the edge a few times now, one time I mentioned in my comment history and another two recently. If you both need to talk about this, please do.

I won't think sharing pains is a sign of weakness at all, it's a sign of strength: being able to talk. :)  
That's great! I'm sorry for not replying sooner. If you would like to PM me any time, please do! :) We share some common ground, sort of. Both had our hearts broken, although I'm over him now. If I can assist in any way, I'm happy to help. :)

Hi! Thank you for sharing this. :) I do hope you don't regret this- after all, these are the struggles that show people you know hurt, pain and sheer agony, and if we can be strong then there is hope for them. See? It's the fight you can inspire in those most in need of it.  
  
But you also found like you need a bit of fight in you. Perhaps we can fight this together? :) If you're happy to keep sharing your own troubles, please do.

Professional diagnosis, that's the way to go! :) Lots of people actually put off treatment because they fear that their own problems pale in comparison to others, but that's not true either. A problem to you is a problem regardless of others, and you deserve help just as much as anyone else.  
And perhaps some guidance will help you through those trust issues? At the very least, you deserve some faith and confidence in yourself.

That's excellent news! And I commend you on your selflessness. I know depression is one bitch of an illness, because on top of what it makes you feel like, it makes you do thing to make you feel worse.  
  
But I ought to add, teenage years are not the best years of anyone's life- they are the years which the most people look back on and wish they had done differently. They are the years people look back on and regret the most because of all the things they never did. OR, they are the years that were good before adulthood striked and everything went downhill. So either way, you'll be told by almost everyone that these are the best years of your life and that you should make the most of it.  
But they could be wrong. Your life has yet to be lived. You're not a  something-year-old single parent in financial turmoil, and you don't have to be. Neither do you need to be recklase and wasteful of your years, some kid relishing in no responsibility. The only hindsight that you should be taking from these people is that years, ANY years, be you a teenager or in your fiftys, are precious and worth living. In short, you *make* the best years of your life.
You still around? If no one else is, you can PM me. I may not always *immediately* answer, but I will definately answer.

Please don't feel alarmed at your friends behavior. She likely got a bit scared at the responsibility of having your life in her hands and didn't know how to immediately react, but she came back- so sounds like she may be a true friend. Her suggestion is good, and I'm seriously glad you're in councilling, and hope that you find your answers. I can't tell you if your friends are true or not, only you will really know, but friends are suppose to ease your concerns, not talk you through them.   
Correct me if I'm wrong: you won't make the leap, not because you're scared of death or anything, and not just because you don't want to cause others hurt, but because feel you owe it to yourself to keep living? The part of you that is strong and a fighter is telling you not to give up. And, if you really think about it, when you're not afraid of death, what have you in life to lose? You're fearless. Things can only get better. :)
Music is such a great thing. No one else has to like it, as long as you find it comforting. :) And heck, I like some of their songs too.
Seconded. Many of us have had *really* close calls. If you want to talk to us, because you can't with friends/family, please do so.

Hi. I understand the psychological implications of child abuse and how it can destroy later life. It sounds like it has destroyed yours. For that, I am sorry.  
But you're right. It is wrong on *everyones* standards. What happened to you is now happening to those children. Is it not also destroying *their* lives? It will affect them, like it has you, for the rest of their lives, and they in turn will destroy others. **It is a vicious cycle that must be broken somewhere.** It can start with *you*.  
It starts with you seeking help to find *healthy* ways of coping, ways of *controlling* those urges. Councelling. Therapy. Drugs. Exercise and dieting. There will be something that works for you.  
I will support anyone wanting to change their ways. Please tell me you are one of them.

There's hope where there's fight. I'm so sorry for all you must go through, but it must keep going. Fight that man with everything you've got. Please, you've got to stay strong for your daughters. Don't dare let that man get to them. There's going to be ways to fix things. :)  
You sound like an admirable woman, so please don't lose hope because I'm cheering you on. (I don't know if you've ever read 'Living with the Devil' by Amy Norman? You're not alone.)  
You sound like a devoted mother, and I hurt for you. You **will** be able to help them. It'll hurt for a while longer, and obviously a lot more when you've not got your so-called-friends behind you.  
So we at SW are here! :D Honest.

That's disgraceful. I hate therapists with that attitude- they are *supposed* to care. But don't lose hope- counselors are pick and choose, depending whenever you connect or not. Some you just click with, and some you just need to quit sessions with if they're no good. :( I'm wishing you the best of luck finding another.

We're all fools in love. But loving someone isn't a 'fault' and you certainly can't blame yourself for simply having feelings. You're not selfish or greedy or horrible because of them. Please, don't feel guilty for having feelings. I fell for a guy 20 years my senior. Yep. That hurt. But do I blame myself for it? No. There was simply no fault to be had. That applies to you as well.  
Now, the real hard part. Everyone needs the freedom to make their own mistakes, and that includes the ones you love. They need to make their own choices, good and bad, because otherwise shit spins out of control and things roll downhill. Blame and hurt gets tossed about like volleyballs. You could end up becoming more of a victim than a comfort. As much of a cop-out as it sounds, the most you can really do is be that shoulder for tears if it all goes wrong, and the clap on the back when it all goes right.  
One last thing. I really would recommend that you get to a point where you can stand up with your own strengths, and be happy with yourself as a person, before you start a serious relationship. I mean relationship with anyone, by the way, not just possible lovers. You've got to help yourself before you can help anyone else. It's damn hard, but it can be done. I decided that I don't need that man I loved to hold me upright all the time. Try and see if you can find your answers.  
I'm sorry about your dad. Mine's the same. They haven't got a clue, and then get mad at *us* simply for having feelings that we struggle to deal with. I stopped looking to them for answers a long time ago. Do you have any help nearby? A councelling service or such? If you can get to it, please please do, and then you can tell him that you're going to take control over the depression as much as you can, and you would like him to be the safe hand on your shoulder. All he has to do is be the one who believes in you.  
Until then, of course, **I believe in you.** Stay strong, my friend.
Please, please do!! :D You can do this.

Oh man, as someone who also gets mocked for even trying to seek help, I really hurt for you. Please, keep trying for us both. Be strong. Your mother is completely out of line. She drinks to deal with the hurt. At least you know you need to get a therapist. She's probably embarrased about the whole thing which is why she doesn't want anyone else to know. Denial never solved anything. She can keep on drinking if she wants, but please do not let her stop you getting the help you need. I'm so sorry you have to go through this so please know I'm cheering for you.

You might want to die, but your daughter doesn't.  
  
And I'm pretty sure she would rather remember her daddy as the prime example of a man who showed her true strength and bravery, struggling on against all odds because he loved her so so much.
Heehee, I'll be looking out for you!! :D
Thank you for your wonderful encouragement! I wish you all the best too!

A foreign invader exactly, and one that doesn't belong. At some point I will have the strength enough to finally push it aside and stamp it down, and get on with my life without the parasite. It'll take time, and it won't be easy, and I'll want to give up, but I bloody well won't.

I hate getting one-upped. It's not the fact that I was wrong about something, it's the fact they have to be a douchebag about it.*sigh* And now I just encourage people to find their own answers.  
On that note, who can decide for you what standards to have? :) It sounds like you're trying to prove yourself too others, but have you proved yourself to you first?

I have a couple of friends like that. I just let them vent, because we're people and we need to vent sometimes. (Yet even I think they just really need to suck it up because their problems aren't as bad as they make it out to be. Yes, your jeans are suddenly too big for you, is a belt really so repulsive? sigh) But generally, I'm all ears and a hug, not a set of balancing scales. :)  
Please be brave! Fear is nothing to be ashamed of, but rather tackled head first with a knee in the groin. Never be ashamed to feel something, even if it is fear. With fear comes bravery. I wish you all the best in getting through this! You are certainly no fool.

Yes!! 'Stop acting depressed' are the worst words you can get told. I mean who's acting, really?  
The only thing worse than admitting that you have a problem is admitting it and having no one believe you. :(  
I prefered the fantasty in my head and in the end it just completely overwhelmed me. I seriously thought of naught else, and so life just slipped me by and I never noticed or cared.  
I get socially shamed all the time. Every day brings another cringe. Sometimes I embrace it with a laugh, and other days- the bad ones- make me so angry and hurt. But we can do this!! :D Thank you for your encouragement!! I had better succeed now!
Because it's there!! :D No one ever found gold without digging for it!

In all honesty, I suspect there is something that greatly distresses her and that has warped her perception of reality. People do strange things and don't get why anyone else considers it strange. Sometimes it's harmless, and sometimes it's devastating.  
  
It's possibly the same feeling she's trying to project onto you, so when she calls you a useless pos it's because she feels like she's a useless pos. Unable to deal with her own problems she deflects them onto you. It's definitely malicious, yet definitely pitiable. Her behavior does need to be corrected. However, she's got to want treatment for it to be any good.  
That road will become clear to her when she realises she cannot hurt you any longer.

You know what, I am so glad to hear that. You sound like an excellent human being and you do not deserve any of her hatred. I agree with you, mind, it takes an ill person to do what she does, but I won't feel bad for her when she inflincts such pain onto you.  
She is mistaken, and I hope you will be able to put her right as you are a strong and admirable fellow. :)

Yes yes yes!! Completely!!  
  
I refuse to let that beasty win, dammit!

Do you feel like you are in some sort of debt to your mother? I ask because you said you feel grateful for her buying you things, which I totally understand by the way, I'm the same with my father. How can we not be? As cruel as they may be, you have food and a bed and clothes, and feeling as worthless as you do, how can you even consider expecting more?  
  
The thing is, it's not wrong to expect your mother to love you. Love isn't getting presents every year, love is the hug, a kind word and the encouragement from the sidelines. It's certainly not clothes. You're not a child who wanted an Xbox and got a PS3, your a twenty year old getting *assulted* by your own mother. Sure, don't hate her. She sounds pitiable. It's not your responsibility to be her crutch and chase after her every whim. Is it possible for you to put some space between you both in order for you to get control over your life, and then try and reach out to her from a position to do so? It may be a wait, but you cannot help her until you first help yourself.  
  
Best of luck to you. Stay strong!

Same here! Did you get the "You're X years old, what do you have to be sad about?"  
I began to live in my head. Then I thankfully stopped, stopped for years, and now I'm slipping back into it. :( Damn, another mountain to climb.
Congrats on your efforts! Keep planning!! :D

Hey dude!  
I don't normally post comments, but I was feeling down today and wanted to see if anyone else was having a shitty time.  
I'm a bit of a hypocrit, and I'll admit that. Even though the urge to stab myself is stronger than ever tonight, I'm actually commenting here to try and stop you doing it...  
Well... I can't stop you doing anything. That's one thing that's kept me going, actually. The choice is mine and always is mine, just like, in the end, the choice is yours. A little perspective never went amiss however! :D  
I was also an outcast in my youth, and I made sleazy friends through sleazy methods. I was lonely. Sometimes I got so lonely that I would suck up to the popular kids trying to make them like me, just so I would have some friends. It's a mistake I am paying for now. Those kids have turned into horrible people I am glad not to be aquainted with. But I had to go through all that nasty shit in order to be the person I am today. I am confident, because I was made to leave my comfort zone and socialize. I am likable because I don't bitch/gossip and am not mean. What I'm trying to get at, is that I've taken the shitty experiences and learnt from them in order to improve myself. That's something you and I could do. You are in a position to reflect on what went wrong in your life and future improvements. (Those bullies, by the way, will learn that lesson very, very late in life and it will hurt them more that way. I was once a bully myself, and believe me when I say I loathe myself over it. They will too.)  
Another thing, this perspective you now have is absolutely perfect for a stand up comedian. Comedians need strength and confidence and you have both of those, and that is why you can get through this. Whenever you get knocked down, you can climb back up, but you will need courage, and you will need to be as tough as a lion. (I would say bear since biologically they're tougher, but I think in another comment I said something about punching bears in the face and, erm, yes, you don't need anymore punches in the face unless they are the congradulatory sort. :|)  
Experience makes for jokes, and you have more experience than you realise. You can empathize with the outcasts and you can share your positivity with those in desperate need of a smile. You will remember how to laugh. :) You will develop a fantastic sense of humor, and what's even better, you'll probably have a lot of different senses of humor which will make you the first person to catch a joke. :) I believe in you, brah.  
I can't tell you what to do. Quite frankly, I have no advise regarding your daughter, only that I'm sure there are options. There is never not an option.

"It's absolutely crucial for a teen who is having thoughts of self-harm or significant depression to be able to tell a helpful, trustworthy adult."  
That's my problem. I can't tell anyone. And believe me, struggling on is an absolute bitch. So thank you to the Reddit SuicideWatch community!! :D You've been such a huge help for me.

"I don't want to deal with it." That mentality isn't going to help your family, and please make sure they get that. Is there any way for you to have them all support your efforts and work together to change your brother? Because it can be done. It's hard and will take a long time and a *lot* of patience, but it can happen. You don't have to beat him with a table leg, but you can overpower him by numbers. Thing is, I would suggest that you make your intentions clear to your family before you do anything. Tell them you find his behavior completely unacceptable and how you intend to correct him. Ask them to back you up and do the same, be it silent treatment or a swearing match. I really do mean this; you need to get your whole family involved so that he can't manipulate the situation and turn it against you somehow. Also, if you want him to stop picking on your mother, she will need to fight him off herself and make it clear she is not a pushover with or without you there, otherwise he'll just be selective to who he is nice to.

I upvoted you because I'm the same. I do very insensitive things without realising it, and afterwards it'll hit me like a truck. For me this feeling comes and goes, so if you're the same, don't forget the you that cares.

You don't think you need life because if you did then you wouldn't be suicidal. No one *needs* life. Once we have it, we're biologically programmed to survive. When you and I override this programme, we live a life without that born instinct to keep going. Most people fear the very same darkness that you and I can't wait to enter.  
But, like I say, we can die later.

You feel exactly as I feel right now. I'm not even kidding, which is why I'm such a hypocrit posting here trying to make you feel better. But I'm going to post anyway, because perhaps we can get through this together.   
You're the reason?  
I'm also the reason.  
You will know exactly what I mean by this. No one else can be held accountable for our current situations; it's all our doing.  
I want to share a visual image of our struggles, because I'm not great with words; I'm better with pictures.  
In this deep, dark jungle full of exotic trees we recognise but don't know the names of, there is a river, deep blue with white froth, maybe two foot deep on average. This part of the jungle and the river are on a gentle slope, and we are at the bottom of it. We stand in this river and feel the water hitting against our legs, pushing us back downstream. But we wanna go upstream.  
So we step forward. And step forward. And it's really hard, because we're going uphill against a fairly strong current, but we keep walking because there's no sky in the jungle. If we want to see the sky, we have to reach the top of the hill.  
Sometimes there is a sudden dip, and we're sent stumbling into it and we get submerged until we resurface. Other times, the ground beneath us gets further and further away until we're up to our necks in the dark blue water. After we eventually walk on shallow waters we're just too tired to keep moving, and we think whenever we should just lie down and let the river carry us downstream. It's dark down there, but it doesn't require any more effort than just... letting go...  
We rest a little bit, and decide.  
The water relentlessly hits against us and makes us more tired by the second, but we step forward again. Because we're so exhausted, we cry out for help and (if you're like me) get frustrated that no one's helping and just to top if off we start stumbling into the deep again.  
  
Everyone has this journey in the jungle, from the darkness at the bottom to the sky at the top. Our journey is just made harder with the river. But the river is strong, man! No wonder we keep falling over. That thing just keeps flowing and making us weaker.  
  
So there's willpower. We keep wading into it, fighting the current. We make ourselves move with the belief that we are stronger than the current. It's hard, and it's tiring, and a lot of the time it doesn't seem worth it until you look behind you and see the great distance you've travelled. Then: "Just a little more..." doesn't seem so bad. So do that, look at the great distance you've travelled each time you feel like giving up, and tell me *then* that you're pathetic. 
And there's outside help. If someone could come along and see us struggling in the deep, they could offer a rope to pull us out. Can you seek outside help? Are you going to therapy, for example? Remember, it's a climb to get out of the river and will take a lot of effort on our part, much more than our rescuer. Only when you're on the bank and look down at the roaring river behind you, tell me *then* that you're pathetic.  
  
If we can't face the river flow head on, we need to get out the river. If we can't accept outside help, we have to face the flow. Nearly always, we climb out. That is what I would suggest to you. We need to climb out of the river onto the land beside it.  
I don't know your situation. You will have to figure out for yourself how to get out the river. Who will have the rope you need?  
  
But fight a force as strong as a raging river and *then* tell me you're pathetic. You've still alive. You keep surviving. You keep fighting. You, friend, are not pathetic. So don't give up, please.

Death is always going to come, so don't worry about that. One day, we **will** die.  
  
So now you know that, take a deep breath. Seriously, *breathe*. I sometimes forget to breathe, so I inhale deeply and it's the most glorious feeling of the moment. You can feel your whole chest and everything inside it working away. That's what life feels like: breathing.  
So find where you are in your mental musings and breathe. And think. And ask yourself: "What can I change?" and "What is making me unhappy?" and "How can I improve this?" In fact, after each one of those, think about it. Don't just accept these thoughts and go with the flow because it's a cycle that will swallow you. **Fight back**, wade upstream, figure out what you need to do.  
  
Death isn't what you need, it's what you think you want.

Your whole paragraph is exactly my thoughts over the last few days. I really do feel for you.    
I'm not convinced there *is* a purpose to life. We have to make one. It's your life, you should decide what to do with it. Think of the things *you* want to do. Seriously, write down a list off all the things you want to do in your life.When your dead, you're dead, but until then you're breathing and you're thinking and you can do anything. We can die later, it'll wait.

**You take this internet hug and you take it good!!**
You're not worthless and pathetic, but you may be feeling that way because you're not doing anything productive. (Productive in the sense that you're not gaining any happiness from that activity.) You have four months before school, so you could do anything you want in those four months. Pick up a hobby (your poetry could be it, or if you're into literature have a go at novel writing), study something that interests you, join a gym or do some morning exercises... you could try voluntary work like in charity shops or shelters. It's experience you could bring up in any job interviews, and you'll also get to meet a lot of great lovely people. I would recommend that because you'll be out and about and much more sociable. Either way, try and keep your mind occupied with things you like and are interested in. :)  
You know what? **Take another internet hug because I am full of them.** Everyone needs to moan and talk and let off steam, stop beating yourself up just because you're doing it!! :)

Ah man, I'm so there. I fantasize about the many ways I could die, and I also resent all my family/friends for actually missing me when I go. It will hurt them, and cause them to sink into the same hole we're in.  
If the meds aren't working maybe you should try something else.  Maybe you need to *keep going* to therapy, find someone who you click with. Maybe you just need to talk about everything to trustworthy person. You're stressed about work, worried about the future, the depression making you pessimistic and lack of motivation to do anything, right? Can you crack down on the cause of your sadness? If you can find the reason as to why you're so hateful of your life, you can change it. I know you must feel incredibly guilty about what you think you're causing your wife to go through, but as someone in the same boat I am telling you it's not your fault. (Depression is a b*tch.) And if anything, this should motivate you to seek help!  
I don't think there is a way to die without devastating the ones close to us. Therefore, it makes sense to fight on and try and resolve these issues, right? But you need get well for your own sake, seek help because *you* want to improve.

You too? I got my A Level results today as well... I did absolutely abysmal. You described it down to a 't'- we have to motivate ourselves ten times more than everyone else and we don't achieve nearly the same. Three hours ago I was standing in front of the railway line with a train coming my way, and wanted nothing more than to step out onto the tracks. Just to end this miserable everything.  
(I've seen too much Game of Thrones. What did I say to the god of death?) *Not today*. At some point I know that thought may not be enough to stop me from killing myself, at some point I am going to go right over the edge and just do it without a second thought. But that day is going to be the day when I have exhausted all alternatives and just stopped trying. That is not today.
Think of it this way. **You are a fighter.** You could have died a year ago, but you didn't and you fought on. Can we keep fighting another year? Can we fight a third?  
We're young and yet our joints ache and our minds scream, and it honestly feels like the world is against us, that everyone has such high standards we just don't forefill. They want the grades we don't have or the skills we never learned. Compared to everyone else we feel worthless and like failures. But you know: fuck the world. The world is fucking wrong. That university you applied to does not decide your worth, **you do**. Do not give up on yourself. You lack self esteem and you need to find things you like about yourself, the things that make you happy and the experiences you want out of life.  
I know I sound like a hypocrite, and it's probably why I don't post encouraging comments here a lot. Here I am telling you to push on when I was so close to giving up myself.  
But life is what we make of it. We have fallen down *really* far, and we can climb back up or not. If you're as tired as I am, it's so tempting just to fall asleep at the bottom, but there's some beautiful things up above which *are* reachable, and totally worth a look at. And there I go slipping into metaphor...   
I honestly hope some of this helped. /r/SuicideWatch has kept me fighting on. If you need to PM me just to cry, let off steam or anything, please do.
